shownAssessments.comment: Quiet breathing, a slow head glance and small ear and tail accents retain the previous resting personality on the new shape. All four paws remain supported and the shell keeps its form. The six-second phrase is restrained and predictable.

At 0.7 studs/s, the four-beat walk shows separate reach, plant and recovery while the shell remains balanced. The whole-paw weights remove the former cuff penetration. Its long support and short recovery suit the heavy round silhouette. Tight turns still slide and are outside this straight-preview pass.

At 16 studs/s the diagonal pairs produce a distinct quick bound, lifted recovery and short support. The 0.202125-second cycle matches travel without a cadence cap, and the face and shell remain stable. The broad belly coat compresses at maximum reach; small-size and faster catch-up cadence remain limitations.

At the nominal 19.14645 studs/s, the longer stride and quicker 0.18119-second cycle read as more urgent pursuit than Walk. Foot recovery clears the floor and the shell stays quiet. This source view omits the native narrowed-lid overlay; actual guardian speed remains player-relative. Turning and acceleration are not passed by this excerpt.

At the displayed 8 studs/s, alternating contralateral paw pairs row through a smooth 1.6-second phrase with a quiet shell and modest paw feathering. The paddle differs from the land gaits. The preview uses the marked review stage rather than water, and the broad shell hides parts of the far-side strokes.

shownAssessments.comment: At 0 studs/s: The face, shell and separated claw shapes stay readable, with a small head and body movement that keeps the creature alive. shownAssessments.reviewScope: Current offline shown preview. Full movement and developer approval remain separate.

shownAssessments.comment: At 16 studs/s: The tucked posture and larger leg changes distinguish the action from the slower Walk, and the head remains readable. At 16 stud/s the retained short stride repeats about 13.02 cycles/s. The crowded legs flicker and churn beneath a comparatively rigid body, with no convincing weight transfer or readable footfalls. At 50 fps there are fewer than 4 frames per cycle, which also limits contact inspection.
shownAssessments.reviewScope: Current offline shown preview. Full movement and developer approval remain separate.

shownAssessments.comment: At 2.1181 studs/s: The face and shell remain stable and the visible walking branches stay recognisable through the slow cycle. At 2.1181 stud/s, the small leg shuffle does not convincingly support the sustained travel. The body appears to glide relative to the ground marks, with little readable loading and recovery in this view.
